paper: Almgren & Chriss (2000), Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions
application: Reconstruct decision-mid to broker-fill basis points from stored quotes. This measures execution quality including spread; it does not fit market impact or implement institutional TWAP/VWAP without depth/volume data.
Treat volatility as time-varying; compare current conditional risk with sample volatility. No constant-volatility assumption is used to promise returns.
The cited1992 cross-sectional study precedes the1993 three-factor model. A full factor regression needs validated factor series and sufficient account history; no alpha estimate is fabricated.

paper: Gatheral SVI; Gatheral & Jacquier (2014), Arbitrage-free SVI volatility surfaces
application: SVI fitting alone does not ensure an arbitrage-free surface. Explicit restrictions and liquid option-chain prices are needed. The present bot trades underlying assets, so no SVI trading model is enabled.

paper: Avellaneda & Stoikov (2008), High-frequency trading in a limit order book
application: Inventory-aware market making requires limit-order-book, queue and latency information. Broker snapshot quotes are insufficient; this evaluator does not claim high-frequency market-making capability.

paper: Kyle (1985), Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading
application: The original title uses Insider Trading. Kyle lambda cannot be identified from these daily candles alone; signed order flow and price-impact data are required.
Compute excess-return Sharpe only after60 complete daily returns, using dated USD cash proxies and365 calendar-day annualization. Do not annualize a few hours of performance.

Report current-holdings correlations and covariance risk contributions with10% diagonal shrinkage, aligned USD returns and coverage checks. No unstable mean-variance expected-return optimizer controls trades.

Fit a stationary GARCH(1,1) finite parameter grid to at least126 current-holdings proxy returns. Display conditional volatility and a normal-model tail scenario; this is not an out-of-sample validated loss limit.

paper: Carhart (1997), On Persistence in Mutual Fund Performance
application: Show12-minus1-month momentum where253 observations exist. This is not a full four-factor regression, proof of manager skill, or evidence of a dependable monthly return.
